questions.q: Describe the main features of the 73rd Amendment relating to local government.
answer: The 73rd Amendment of 1992 gave constitutional status to rural local government, the Panchayati Raj system, and laid down its main features.

answer.text: It provided a uniform three-tier structure of panchayats at the village, block and district levels, namely the Gram Panchayat, the Panchayat Samiti and the Zilla Parishad. At the base is the Gram Sabha, the assembly of all the voters of a village.

Elections to these bodies are held regularly every five years and are conducted by an independent State Election Commission. Seats are reserved for Scheduled Castes and Tribes in proportion to their population, and at least one-third of all seats are reserved for women.
A State Finance Commission is set up every five years to review the financial position of the panchayats.

answer: These features have deepened democracy at the grassroots and empowered weaker sections and women.

questions.q: Why is local self-government important, and how does it deepen democracy?

answer.text: means governance by elected local bodies — panchayats in villages and municipalities in towns — and it brings democracy close to the people.

list: Local problems like water, roads and sanitation are best understood and solved by local people
It lets ordinary citizens take part directly in decisions that affect their daily lives
It draws large numbers of people, including women and the marginalised, into public life
It trains citizens in self-rule and makes government more responsive and accountable at the grassroots

questions.q: How did the 73rd and 74th Amendments strengthen local government in India?

answer.text: of 1992 gave local government a firm constitutional footing, making it a genuine third tier of government.

list: They made a three-tier system of panchayats in rural areas and municipalities in urban areas mandatory
They required regular elections to these bodies every five years

answer.lead: They also made them more representative.
answer.text: Seats were reserved for the marginalised.

list: One-third of seats were reserved for women, and seats for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in proportion to their population
A State Election Commission and Finance Commission were provided, giving local bodies real standing
